section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the concept of "taking the stones of the place" applies within man himself, where letters are like stones—the inanimate level of his faculties—yet they draw down a very exalted light, analogous to how the "utterance of G-d" in bread is higher in its source than that in man.
section.t: A)
Now, the matter of "And he took from the stones of the place, etc." also exists within man himself.
And the explanation is,
for it is known82
that stones are letters83,
for just as stones are inanimate, so too are letters the aspect of the inanimate within man's faculties.
But nevertheless,
and for this very reason,
they draw down
(letters, from the term "ata"84
"boker"85,
a concept of drawing down)
an aspect of a most exalted light.
And analogous to what is known86
in the explanation of the verse87
"For not by bread alone does man live, but by every utterance of the mouth of G-d does man live,"
that the fact that bread sustains man is because the utterance of the mouth of G-d within the bread
(the vegetative)
is more exalted
(in its source)
than the utterance of the mouth of G-d within man,
for this very descent to a lower level indicates that in its source it is more exalted,
for whatever is higher descends lower,
so too is it regarding the matter of letters,
the inanimate
(within man),
whose source is higher even than the aspect of the vegetative88,
for whatever is higher
descends lower and lower.
And this is the matter of "And he took from the stones of the place and placed them at his headrest"
(as it is in the service of each and every Jew),
that the service of the aspect of letters,
the inanimate within man,
reaches higher than the service of the aspect of intellect
("at his headrest").

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two interpretations of "taking the stones of the place"—service of the inanimate within man and the refinement of physical things of the world—are connected, as the refinement of the physical world is accomplished through the inanimate within man, specifically the power of speech and primarily action.
section.t: B)
And the two aforementioned explanations of "And he took from the stones of the place, etc."
[the service of the aspect of the inanimate within man
(above, section 11)
and the service of refining physical things of the world
(above, section 9)]
are related to each other.
For the refinement of the matters of this physical world
(the stones of the place of the world)
is accomplished through the inanimate within man,
the power of speech,
and primarily—the power of action90,
for action is the main thing91.
And one should add,
that the connection of these two matters is not only from the aspect of the "lower" element
(stone,
inanimate)
within them
[that the action in the physicality of the world is through the lower faculties within man],
but rather,
also regarding the matter of the elevation within them
("and placed them at his headrest").
That is,
that it is within the power of each and every Jew to make from his portion in the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,
for His very Essence92,
is because through his service with his lower faculties, the essence of the soul, which is united with His Essence, blessed be He, is revealed93.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the service of the inanimate within man, which reaches above the "head" of Yaakov (the level of Chayah), reveals the level of Yechidah within him, which is the essential self-sacrifice that every Jew possesses, as it is beyond any opposition.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in many places94
regarding the matter of the yud of the Name Havayah within the soul of man, which is the aspect of Chayah.
And since the aspect of the head of Yaakov
[which is the yud of Yaakov,
which is the yud of the Name Havayah
(as above, section 4)]
is the aspect of Chayah,
it is understood from this,
that this that the service of the aspect of the inanimate within man reaches above the aspect of the head of Yaakov
(as above
(at the end of section 11)
in the explanation of "And he took from the stones of the place and placed them at his headrest"),
the intention in this is—that through the service of the aspect of the inanimate within man,
the aspect of Yechidah within him is revealed
(which is above the aspect of Chayah).
For the matter of the service of the aspect of the inanimate within man,
is that even though he has no vitality whatsoever
(neither from the feeling of the emotions of the heart,
nor from the intellect of the mind,
and also not from the will that is above intellect
(the aspect of Chayah))
nevertheless he performs his service,
it is from his very essence,
that each Jew, in his essential being, wants to do everything that is the will of G-d,
as per the well-known ruling of the Rambam95.
And this is that each and every Jew,
even the most lowly of the lowly,
can give his life for the sanctification of G-d's Name96,
for the power of self-sacrifice is from his essence, the aspect of Yechidah97,
for regarding this level, no opposition applies,
"the faintest reflection has no hold on them"98.
[And this is also what the Torah promised, that ultimately Israel will repent, etc., and immediately they will be redeemed99,
that the intention of "ultimately Israel will repent" is
(also)
for each and every Jew100
— for upon the aspect of Yechidah within each Jew, no opposition applies, G-d forbid, except that it is in concealment,
and the Torah of Truth promises that ultimately it will be revealed].
